cases.prompt: Drive three simultaneous sample inputs from one 1 MHz timing reference. Each input adds 18 pF and every sample edge must settle monotonically within 120 ns.

Transfer a precision control value across a functional isolation boundary while keeping the two returns independent. A single loss-of-power event must force the receiving side to a bounded safe value.
Distribute a 12 MHz clock to one controller and four logic receivers with 55 pF aggregate loading. Bound edge rate, startup state, and receiver voltage compatibility.
Carry reset, interrupt, and enable signals between 1.2 V and 3.3 V domains. Reset and enable are one-way, interrupt may be open-drain, and neither side may back-power the other.

Support two-wire programming and runtime debugging for a low-power controller. The same pins serve application GPIO after startup and the external tool may remain connected while the target is unpowered.
Provide a four-signal debug connection for a 1.8 V controller while a 3.3 V host is attached. Preserve boot-state requirements and prevent contention with shared application functions.
Send a 16-bit control value and return a fault indication across a 1 kV functional isolation boundary. Both sides can start independently and any missing supply must produce a defined safe state.
Acquire a 5 V serial sensor from a 1.8 V controller at 8 MHz while also accepting a 3.3 V open-drain alarm. Enforce direction, loading, supply-loss, and startup-state limits.
Generate an isolated 12 V rail at 250 mA from a 24 V industrial source. Limit inrush, tolerate output short circuit, and discharge the output below 2 V within 500 ms after shutdown.
Generate 1.8 V at 1.5 A from a 3.3 V source. Hold deviation within 4 percent during a 1 A load step and prove junction temperature and transient current remain within reviewed limits.
Connect six open-drain sensors split between 1.8 V and 3.3 V supplies at 1 MHz. Aggregate bus capacitance is 360 pF and disconnected sensor branches must not disable the remaining bus.
Read a 5 V push-pull motion sensor from a 1.8 V controller over a 1 m cable at 4 MHz. The controller may be unpowered while the sensor remains active.
